draft_key_information_units.information: Group revenue and profitability declined significantly in 2025 compared to 2024, with revenue falling 42.3% to EUR 310.9 million, gross profit decreasing to EUR 55.9 million (18.0% margin) from EUR 95.9 million (17.8% margin), operating profit dropping to EUR 34.3 million (11.0% margin) from EUR 72.5 million (13.4% margin), and net profit attributable to equity holders falling to EUR 39.9 million from EUR 64.7 million.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: KEY INDICATORS table showing Revenue (million EUR) 310.9 (2025) vs 539.0 (2024); Gross profit 55.9 (2025) vs 95.9 (2024); Operating profit 34.3 (2025) vs 72.5 (2024); Net profit 39.9 (2025) vs 64.7 (2024).

draft_key_information_units.information: The 2025 revenue decline was driven by the completion of major projects initiated in prior years during 2025, combined with a slower pace of new contract signing in 2024 and the first half of 2025; this project cycle effect compressed profitability despite eventual improvement in contract signing activity later in 2025.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman: 'In 2024, we were engaged in several large projects that had been started in earlier years, and these were completed as planned during 2025. The pace of signing new contracts was slower in 2024 and in the first half of 2025.'

draft_key_information_units.information: A major improvement in contract signing during the second half of 2025 resulted in the execution of Merko's largest-ever contracts for the Rūdninkai defence campus in Lithuania, which will contribute gradually to revenue starting in 2026 and provide stable workload for years ahead.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman: 'the second half of 2025 showed a clear improvement, and preparatory efforts resulted in new major contracts... signing of the largest contracts in Merko’s history for the construction of two phases of the Rūdninkai defence campus... will begin to contribute to revenue gradually in 2026 and onwards.'

draft_key_information_units.information: The company expanded its public-private partnership (PPP) business through new real estate development agreements signed in 2025 for the Krulli quarter (Tallinn) and Uus-Karlowa quarter (Tartu), alongside continued success in the Noblessner area, enhancing long-term workload stability and diversification.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman: 'Alongside the successful real estate development partnership in the Noblessner area of Tallinn, we signed two similar cooperation agreements in 2025 for the development of the Krulli quarter in Tallinn and the Uus-Karlowa quarter in Tartu. The Rūdninkai project marks a significant expansion of our PPP business Lithuania.'

draft_key_information_units.information: Strategic investment in network companies operating under the Connecto brand delivered exceptional returns, accounting for one quarter (25%) of Merko's consolidated net profit in 2025 and substantially expanding operations in Latvia and Lithuania.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman: 'A strategic decision made several years ago to invest in network companies operating under the Connecto brand has also clearly proven its value... in 2025 this investment in the joint venture accounted for as much as one quarter of Merko’s consolidated net profit.'

draft_key_information_units.information: Residential construction activity surged due to improved consumer confidence across the Baltic region, with apartment construction starts exceeding three times the 2024 level, leading to 358 apartments sold (EUR 67.8 million) compared to 323 apartments (EUR 58.9 million) in 2024 and inventory buildup to 1,169 units.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman: 'in 2025 we were able to start construction of more than three times as many new apartments as in 2024.' Operating result section: 'A total of 358 apartments... sold in 2025... compared to 323 apartments... in 2024.'

draft_key_information_units.information: Liquidity decreased with cash and cash equivalents falling to EUR 41.4 million (from EUR 91.9 million), while the equity ratio strengthened to 62.8% (from 56.9%) and debt ratio remained moderate at 8.0%; dividend payments of EUR 33.6 million impacted financing cash flows.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: CONSOLIDATED STATEMENT OF FINANCIAL POSITION: Cash and cash equivalents 41,424 (2025) vs 91,879 (2024); Equity ratio 62.8% (2025) vs 56.9% (2024); Debt ratio 8.0% (2025) vs 7.5% (2024). PROFIT ALLOCATION PROPOSAL: Dividends (EUR 1.25 per share) 22,125,000 (proposed) and paid 33,630,000.

draft_key_information_units.information: The secured order book increased substantially to EUR 466.9 million from EUR 340.6 million as at end-2024, indicating a robust future revenue pipeline despite 2025's revenue challenges.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: KEY INDICATORS table: Order book (million EUR) 466.9 (2025) vs 340.6 (2024).

evaluation.selection_rationale: These units capture material financial performance changes (D1), key drivers of variance (D2), strategically important new contracts and PPP expansions (D3-D4), high-impact joint venture performance (D5), significant segment growth in real estate development (D6), liquidity and capital position dynamics (D7), and forward-looking order book strength (D8). Each unit represents an independently omittable theme central to understanding Merko's 2025 performance, supported solely by the SOURCE FINANCIAL REPORT. Units D1-D6 align with salience in the REFERENCE SUMMARY; D7 and D8 provide additional material context on liquidity and future outlook not exhaustively covered in the reference but essential for a concise summary.
